card: This pull request cleans up CMake feature detection snippets to eliminate compiler warnings and configures `check_cxx_source_compiles_with_flags()` to treat warnings as errors. It also switches the x86 SHA-NI compiler flag from `-msse4` to `-msse4.1`. This fixes configuration errors and disabled optimizations when building with strict warning flags like `-Werror`, and unblocks native Windows compilation using clang-cl as tracked in #31507.
changed_since_previous: No substantial changes to the approach or scope since the previous review.
evidence: PR description demonstrates build configuration failure when passing `-DAPPEND_CXXFLAGS="-Wall -Werror"`: 'CMake Error at cmake/module/TestAppendRequiredLibraries.cmake:91 (message): Cannot figure out how to use std::atomic.'
PR description demonstrates ARMv8 SHA-NI detection failing under `-Werror=uninitialized` and SSE4.2 detection failing under `-Werror=conversion`

Commit message for 5bb7c5646a: '-msse4 is merely a synonym for -msse4.2 in both GCC and Clang, but it is not accepted by the clang-cl frontend. Furthermore, the x86 SHA-NI code uses only SSE4.1 intrinsics and no SSE4.2 ones.'
problem: When users or build environments pass warning flags such as `-Wall -Werror` via `APPEND_CXXFLAGS`, several CMake introspection snippets fail to compile due to unused variables, uninitialized reads, or implicit conversions, falsely disabling optimizations or failing configuration entirely. Additionally, `check_cxx_source_compiles_with_flags()` previously allowed warnings like `-Wunknown-argument` without failing, and the `clang-cl` compiler rejects `-msse4` even though x86 SHA-NI only requires SSE4.1.

risk.why: A flaw in feature test snippets could erroneously enable or disable CPU hardware acceleration features or fail CMake configuration.

scope_notes: Touches only CMake build scripts and configure-time test compilation snippets.
summary: Updates CMake's `check_cxx_source_compiles_with_flags()` to treat compiler warnings as errors, cleans up compiler warning triggers across several feature detection snippets, and changes the x86 SHA-NI flag from `-msse4` to `-msse4.1`.
